questions.question:
Consider a relation [latex]R( A, B, C, D, E )[/latex] with the following three functional dependencies.
[latex]AB \rightarrow C;BC \rightarrow D; C \rightarrow E;[/latex]
The number of superkeys in the relation [latex]R[/latex] is .
questions.explanation:
A and B never appear on the right side of any FD, so every key must contain A and B.
[latex]AB^+=AB\rightarrow ABC\rightarrow ABCD\rightarrow ABCDE[/latex], so AB is the only candidate key.

Superkeys = AB plus any subset of {C, D, E}: [latex]2^3=8[/latex].

Answer: 8

S2: Given the table R(a,b,c) where a and b together form the primary key, the following is a valid table definition.
CREATE TABLE S (
a INTEGER,
d INTEGER,
e INTEGER,
PRIMARY KEY (d),
FOREIGN KEY (a) references R)

options.B: Both S1 and S2 are TRUE

questions.question:
Consider the following transaction involving two bank accounts x and y.

The constraint that the sum of the accounts x and y should remain constant is that of

options.B: Consistency

Answer: Consistency

questions.question:
Consider a join (relation algebra) between relations r(R)and s(S) using the nested loop
method. There are 3 buffers each of size equal to disk block size, out of which one buffer is
reserved for intermediate results. Assuming size(r(R))[latex]\lt[/latex]size(s(S)), the join will have fewer
number of disk block accesses if

options.A: relation r(R) is in the outer loop.
options.B: relation s(S) is in the outer loop
options.C: join selection factor between r(R) and s(S) is more than 0.5.
options.D: join selection factor between r(R) and s(S) is less than 0.5

questions.explanation:
With one buffer each for the outer and inner relation, block accesses = [latex]b_{outer}+b_{outer}\times b_{inner}[/latex].

The product term is the same either way, so the cost is smaller when the outer relation has fewer blocks. Since r is smaller, put r in the outer loop.

Answer: relation r(R) is in the outer loop

questions.question:
Consider the following schedule S of transactions T1, T2, T3, T4:

Which one of the following statements is CORRECT?

options.A: S is conflict-serializable but not recoverable
options.B: S is not conflict-serializable but is recoverable
options.C: S is both conflict-serializable and recoverable
options.D: S is neither conflict-serializable nor is it recoverable

Order: R2(X), W3(X), C3, W1(X), C1, W2(Y), R2(Z), C2, R4(X), R4(Y), C4.

Conflict edges: T2[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]T3, T2[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]T1, T3[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]T1 (on X), T1[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]T4, T3[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]T4 (on X), T2[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]T4 (on Y). No cycle [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] conflict serializable (T2, T3, T1, T4).

T4 reads X from T1 and Y from T2, and both commit before T4 commits [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] recoverable.

questions.question:
Two transactions [latex]T_1 \; and \; T_2[/latex] are given as:

[latex]T_{1}:r_{1} (X)w_{1}(X)r_{1}(Y)w_{1}(Y) [/latex]
[latex]T_{2}:r_{2}(Y)w_{2}(Y)r_{2}(Z)w_{2}(Z)[/latex]

where [latex]r_{i}(V)[/latex] denotes a read operation by transaction [latex]T_{i}[/latex] on a variable V and [latex]w_{i}(V)[/latex] denotes a write operations by transaction [latex]T_{i}[/latex] on a variable V. The total number of conflict serializable schedules that can be formed by [latex]T_1 \; and \; T_2[/latex] is _____________.
questions.explanation:
T1 = a1 a2 a3 a4 (a3, a4 use Y), T2 = b1 b2 b3 b4 (b1, b2 use Y). The only conflicts are on Y, so a schedule is conflict serializable iff all of T1's Y operations come before T2's, or the other way round.
- T1 before T2 on Y: a4 before b1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] the serial schedule T1 T2: 1 way.
- T2 before T1 on Y: b2 before a3. Of all [latex]\binom84=70[/latex] interleavings, 17 have a3 before b2, so 53 qualify.

Total = 1 + 53 = 54

Answer: 54

questions.question: Consider two relations R1(A,B) with the tuples (1,5), (3,7) and R2(A,C) = (1,7), (4,9). Assume that R(A,B,C) is the full natural outer join of R1 and R2. Consider the following tuples of the form (A,B,C): a = (1,5,null), b = (1,null,7), c = (3, null, 9), d = (4,7,null), e = (1,5,7), f = (3,7,null), g = (4,null,9). Which one of the following statements is correct?

options.A: R contains a, b, e, f, g but not c, d.
options.B: R contains all of a, b, c, d, e, f, g.
options.C: R contains e, f, g but not a, b.
options.D: R contains e but not f, g.

questions.explanation:
Natural join on A:
- A = 1 matches: (1, 5, 7) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] e
- R1 (3, 7) has no match: (3, 7, null) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] f
- R2 (4, 9) has no match: (4, null, 9) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] g

Since A = 1 matched, (1, 5, null) and (1, null, 7) do not appear.

Answer: R contains e, f, g but not a, b

questions.question: Consider a relational database schema with a relation [latex]R(A, B, C, D)[/latex]. If [latex]\{A, B\}[/latex] and [latex]\{A, C\}[/latex] are the only two candidate keys of the relation [latex]R[/latex], then the number of superkeys of relation [latex]R[/latex] is ________. (answer in integer)
questions.explanation:
A superkey is any subset of attributes that contains at least one candidate key as a subset. Here the [latex]4[/latex] attributes are [latex]\{A,B,C,D\}[/latex] and the candidate keys are [latex]\{A,B\}[/latex] and [latex]\{A,C\}[/latex].

Count subsets of [latex]\{A,B,C,D\}[/latex] containing [latex]\{A,B\}[/latex]: freely choose the remaining [latex]\{C,D\}[/latex] → [latex]2^2=4[/latex] subsets.
Count subsets containing [latex]\{A,C\}[/latex]: freely choose the remaining [latex]\{B,D\}[/latex] → [latex]2^2=4[/latex] subsets.
Subsets counted twice are those containing both [latex]\{A,B\}[/latex] and [latex]\{A,C\}[/latex], i.e. containing [latex]\{A,B,C\}[/latex]: freely choose remaining [latex]\{D\}[/latex] → [latex]2^1=2[/latex] subsets.

By inclusion-exclusion, total superkeys [latex]=4+4-2=6[/latex].

Answer: 6

questions.question: Consider a database implemented using B+ tree for file indexing and installed on a disk drive with block size of 4 KB. The size of search key is 12 bytes and the size of tree/disk pointer is 8 bytes. Assume that the database has one million records. Also assume that no node of the B+ tree and no records are present initially in main memory. Consider that each record fits into one disk block. The minimum number of disk accesses required to retrieve any record in the database is _______
questions.explanation:
Checking each statement:
- Internal node order p: [latex]8p+12(p-1)\le4096\Rightarrow p=205[/latex].
- Leaf: [latex]20k+8\le4096\Rightarrow k=204[/latex] keys per leaf.

Leaves for [latex]10^6[/latex] records: [latex]\lceil10^6/204\rceil=4902[/latex]; next level [latex]\lceil4902/205\rceil=24[/latex]; then 1 root. So the tree has 3 levels.

Accesses = 3 (tree) + 1 (record block) = 4

Answer: 4

questions.question:
Consider the following databases chedule with two transactions, T1 and T2.
[latex]S=r_{2}(X);r_{1}(X);r_{2}(Y);w_{1}(X);r_{1}(Y);w_{2}(X);a_{1};a_{2}[/latex]
where [latex]r_{i}(Z)[/latex] denotes a read operation by transaction [latex]T_{i}[/latex] on avariable Z, [latex]w_{i}(Z)[/latex] denotes a write operation by [latex]T_{i}[/latex] on avariable Z and [latex]a_{i}[/latex] denotes an abort by transaction [latex]T_{i}[/latex].
Which one of the following statements about the above schedule is TRUE?

options.A: S is non-recoverable
options.B: S is recoverable,but has a cascading abort
options.C: S does not have a cascading abort
options.D: S is strict

questions.explanation:
No transaction reads a value written by the other before it ends: T1 reads X before T2 writes it, and T2's reads happen before T1's write. So when T1 aborts, T2 does not need to be aborted: no cascading abort.

It is not strict, because [latex]w_2(X)[/latex] overwrites [latex]w_1(X)[/latex] while T1 is still active.

Answer: S does not have a cascading abort

questions.question:
Consider the following relational schema:
Employee (empId, empName, empDept )
Customer (custId,custName, salesRepId, rating)
SalesRepId is a foreign key referring to empId of the employee relation. Assume that each employee makes a sale to at least one customer. What does the following query return?
SELECT empName 
FROM employee E 
 WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT custId
FROM customer C
WHERE C. salesRepId = E. empId
AND C. rating < > 'GOOD')

options.A: Names of all the employees with at least one of their customers having a 'GOOD' rating
options.B: Names of all the employees with at most one of their customers having a 'GOOD' rating.
options.C: Names of all the employees with none of their customers having a 'GOOD' rating.
options.D: Names of all the employees with all their customers having a 'GOOD' rating.

questions.explanation:
The subquery finds this employee's customers whose rating is not 'GOOD'. NOT EXISTS keeps the employee only if there are none.

Since every employee has at least one customer, this means all of the employee's customers are rated 'GOOD'.

Answer: Names of all the employees with all their customers having a 'GOOD' rating

questions.question:
Suppose the following functional dependencies hold on a relation U with attributes [latex]P, Q, R, S, \text{ and } T[/latex]:

[latex]P \rightarrow QR \\ RS \rightarrow T[/latex]

Which of the following functional dependencies can be inferred from the above functional dependencies?

options.B: [latex]R \rightarrow T[/latex]
options.C: [latex]P \rightarrow R[/latex]
options.D: [latex]PS \rightarrow Q[/latex]

questions.explanation:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]P\rightarrow QR[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] [latex]P\rightarrow R[/latex] (decomposition) True
- [latex]PS\rightarrow RS[/latex] (augmentation) and [latex]RS\rightarrow T[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] [latex]PS\rightarrow T[/latex] True
- [latex]P\rightarrow Q[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] [latex]PS\rightarrow Q[/latex] True
- [latex]R\rightarrow T[/latex]: [latex]R^+=\{R\}[/latex], so not implied False

Answer: [latex]PS\rightarrow T,\ P\rightarrow R,\ PS\rightarrow Q[/latex]
